dimensions.assessment: Affects individuals with disabilities aged 18 or older employed by entities holding special wage certificates, as well as employers and state vocational rehabilitation units.
dimensions.evidence: Any... individual with a disability who is... 18 or older... [if] The individual chooses to accept employment with such entity.

dimensions.assessment: Removes pre-employment barriers for young adults entering subminimum wage work and alters compliance conditions for employers seeking state career counseling resources.
dimensions.evidence: eliminates a requirement that an individual with a disability who is age 24 or younger receive pre-employment transition services and meet specified vocational rehabilitation criteria

dimensions.assessment: No significant federal spending or revenue changes are indicated in the source text.
Amends Section 511 of the Rehabilitation Act of 1973 by changing eligibility criteria and exception rules for subminimum wage employment.
dimensions.evidence: Section 511 of the Rehabilitation Act of 1973 (29 U.S.C. 794g) is amended

dimensions.assessment: Permanent change to the Rehabilitation Act of 1973 governing subminimum wage employment prerequisites.
dimensions.evidence: The amendments made by this Act shall apply with respect to the employment of an individual on or after the date of enactment of this Act.

missing_information: The exact number of workers or special wage certificate entities affected is not provided.
importance_detail.rationale: The bill removes the requirement for young adults with disabilities (ages 18-24) to undergo pre-employment transition services and vocational rehabilitation before accepting subminimum wage work, and relaxes state agency career counseling requirements if documented state contact efforts fail.
